altitude.note: Elevation of the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station (NSF: approximately 2,835 m, 9,301 ft). ARA lies about 2 km from IceCube near the station on the same ice surface (ARA overview paper), so the station elevation is used; this is not a separate survey of the ARA stations.
altitude.quote: Sits atop the Antarctic ice sheet at an elevation of approximately 2,835 meters (9,301 feet) above sea level.

coordinates.note: No ARA-specific page publishes station-level latitude/longitude. The NSF Amundsen-Scott station page positions the station at 90 S (the geographic South Pole); the ARA overview paper says only that the five stations are located about 2 km from the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, which the IceCube page places near the station. The geographic South Pole is therefore recorded as an approximate anchor point (lat -90, lon 0) with a generous precision_m to cover the IceCube footprint and ARA's ~2 km offset from it; this is not a surveyed position of the ARA stations.
coordinates.quote: Positioned at 90°S, the geographic South Pole.

depth.quote: deployed at a depth of 100-200 m over the period 2012-2018

name: South Pole — ARA stations
notes: facility_id references facility:amundsen-scott-south-pole-station, owned by the icecube workstream; not created here, per the ID registry and this workstream's brief (ARA is explicitly scoped as 'a new site under the existing facility').

summary.plain: A handful of boreholes near the South Pole, about two kilometres from the IceCube observatory, each holding a small station of radio antennas listening for neutrinos.
summary.technical: ARA station field at the geographic South Pole, ~2 km from the IceCube in-ice array, with stations deployed 100-200 m deep in the ice sheet.
